Brent oil finished out the week at the highest level since April as intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia added to supply concerns already stoked by the US-Iran war.
The global crude benchmark settled below $117 a barrel on Friday, up more than 6% this week, while West Texas Intermediate closed above $103. Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed recent attacks on the Saudi Red Sea port of YanbuBloomberg Terminal
, as well as deadly strikes on an oil field and airport in the kingdom.

For much of this year, Treasuries offered investors little of their traditional protection when technology stocks stumbled. This week, that role has bounced back sharply.
A gauge of the inverse relationship between US government bonds and AI-focused stocks has strengthened to levels last seen a year ago. It’s a sign the deepening tech selloff is sending investors back into bonds for safety, reviving a haven role that had faded as inflation worries and higher interest rates weighed on Treasuries.

A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the Federal Reserve decision on interest rates.
Brent crude topped $116 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened global supplies. The S&P 500 saw back-to-back losses. That’s even as selling pressure on tech firms abated. A gauge of chipmakers rebounded, while still heading toward its longest weekly slide since November. Treasury yields rose after the market’s best day in more than a year.

US states and local governments are selling debt at a record clip, borrowing more than $500 billion so far this year as the need for infrastructure and airport upgrades mounts.
Municipal bond issuance is up almost 6% from the same period last year and is on pace to top $600 billion by year-end, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. In 2025, bond sales crossed the threshold in early November.

By Alex HarrisOctober 23, 2026 at 5:20 PM UTCBookmark
Save
Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
US funding markets risk facing a volatile, last-minute “scramble” to meet a key 2027 deadline for mandatory central clearing of daily transactions, strategists at Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce warned.
Just eight months ahead of the June 2027 deadline, clearing volumes of repurchase agreements have flattened after slowing in the first months of the year, according to a report from the International Swaps and Derivatives Association. The drop is “deeply disheartening,” CIBC strategists led by Michael Cloherty wrote in a note Friday.

item.title: US Consumer Sentiment Slips to Five-Month Low on Inflation
item.description:
Oct 23rd, 2026
US Consumer Sentiment Slips to Five-Month Low on Inflation
US consumer sentiment edged down to a five-month low in October as high prices and rising interest rates depressed morale. The University of Michigan’s final sentiment index eased to 48 from 48.1 in September, according to the survey released Friday. Even so, that was an improvement from the preliminary reading and topped all estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists. Joanne Hsu, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers Director joins to discuss.
